A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Orak, with the same 12-game benchmark, MCP interface and gameplay fine-tuning framework. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite reorganization and additional experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original gameplay evaluations, competitive arenas, agent-module and modality ablations, and fine-tuning generalization results in Tables 3–8 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original gameplay experiments and adds model and human comparisons, non-game evaluations, augmentation sensitivity results and a controlled transfer study.

M1.justification: The MCP pipeline, game interfaces, agent modules, supervised fine-tuning procedure and default ten-paraphrase augmentation remain unchanged. Section 4 restates selection of more than 900 individual inferences as more than 300 three-module sequences; this does not establish a new method.

E1.justification: V2 adds Math500 and WebShop easy/hard evaluations, extending coverage beyond games to mathematics and web interaction (Section 5.6, Table 7). All 12 core games remain. Reported intra-game coverage decreases from six games to five: Super Mario's Stage 3-1 results and Appendix P.3 description disappear, although Figure 28 retains its illustration.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Llama3.3-70B, Qwen2.5-72B, GPT-5 and human novices. Tables 5–6 add Qwen2.5-VL-7B/32B to the modality comparisons. GPT-4o reference rows disappear from the consolidated fine-tuning comparison, although its Street Fighter III reference remains in Appendix C, Table 12. Arena comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 introduces larger model configurations, a three-novice control, augmentation-count variants and training exclusively on Baba Is You for transfer evaluation. Her Story's normalization denominator changes from 272 to 271; Stardew's expert-profit denominator changes from 813 to 956. Default-strategy selection is reported as based on GPT-4o alone rather than GPT-4o and o3-mini, while the selected strategies remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix O results test 0, 3, 10 and 20 augmentations, addressing sensitivity to paraphrase quantity (Table 46). New Appendix Q trains only on Baba Is You and evaluates six other games to investigate transfer across genres and gameplay requirements (Table 48). These controls were absent from v1; most existing module ablations and qualitative analyses remain.

E5.justification: Matched experiments retain their game-specific run counts and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting, including 20 Super Mario trials and three trials for several other games. No new seed-selection, confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is documented. The added appendix ablations provide point estimates without establishing additional replication.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial model, human, transfer and ablation results. Table 7 newly reports Llama-3.2-3B Math500 scores of 29.6 before fine-tuning and 36.1 afterward, and WebShop-E/H changes from 0.0 to 8.4/12.6. Existing scores also change with normalization: GPT-4o's Stardew score becomes 81.4 instead of 95.7, which is not evidence of worse gameplay. Some fine-tuning reference and Super Mario entries are removed.

T1.justification: Appendices F.3 and J.3 revise explicit normalized-score definitions through the changed clip count and expert-gold reference. J.3 also replaces v1's inconsistent '1013 − 200 = 800' statement with '1156 − 200 = 956.' Trajectory definitions, Bradley–Terry mathematics and other scoring formulations remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The benchmark, MCP interface and expert-trajectory dataset remain the principal contributions. The introduction extends the fine-tuning transfer claim from intra-game and unseen-game generalization to non-game mathematics and web interaction. This broadens one contribution without redefining the central research work.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning model capacity in non-game transfer, diminishing returns from augmentation, and shared reasoning requirements across games. Section 6 newly qualifies the benchmark as favorable to reasoning because states are curated into structured text. Appendix R adds licensing and commercial-use boundaries; the existing latency, audio and reinforcement-learning limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 discloses a collection quota exceeding 1,000 inference sequences per game and adds fine-tuning GPU times in Table 47. Appendix R specifies game-purchase, distribution and research-only use conditions. The four-A100 training recipe, token filtering and final training counts of 105,502 and 87,660 remain unchanged. Detailed protocols for the new non-game evaluations are sparse.

R1.justification: V2 adds LMGame-Bench to Section 2 and Table 1, alongside new citations for Qwen2.5-VL, WebShop, game-design criteria and Bradley–Terry estimation. References including AgentBank, Learn-by-Interact and WebRL are removed. The central positioning around genre coverage, agent-module studies and a fine-tuning dataset remains.

P1.justification: V2 condenses and edits the abstract, introduction and related work, replaces numbered related-work subsections with paragraph headings, and changes Section 6 from Conclusion to Discussion. Earlier limitations and societal-impact material are consolidated in Appendix R. Most method descriptions and game-specific appendix prose remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The main comparison tables gain rows, and v1's separate generalization Tables 7–8 become a combined Table 7 with non-game columns. V2 adds appendix Tables 46–48, revises Table 1's columns, and changes typography, headers and float placement. The overview, pipeline, arena and gameplay illustrations retain their content.

improvement.justification: Larger open-model comparisons and human references partly address v1's limited context for interpreting model performance. The new augmentation and transfer controls also strengthen the evidence behind the fine-tuning dataset, while the structured-state limitation improves transparency. These benefits are constrained by sparse non-game protocols and inconsistent propagation of revised Stardew scores: v2's main Table 4 is updated, but appendix Table 32 retains the old values. The net improvement is useful but limited.
